qa_pairs.question: What is C++ and when was it created?
qa_pairs.answer: C++ is a general-purpose, high-level, multi-paradigm programming language that was created by Bjarne Stroustrup at Bell Labs in 1979 by extending the C programming language.

qa_pairs.question: Are the C and C++ programming languages the same?
qa_pairs.answer: No, the C language is a distinct language from the C++ language. While much C code can be used as-is in C++, there are differences that will affect compilation and/or program execution.

qa_pairs.question: Why is it preferable to compile concurrent C++ code using C++11 or newer standards?
qa_pairs.answer: Prior to 2011, ISO C++ standards had no definitions of concurrency and memory models, meaning pre-C++11 compiled code offered no guarantees concerning the ordering of memory reads and writes under concurrency. Compiling with C++11 or newer ensures well-defined concurrency behaviour and allows taking advantage of optimizations from features like `constexpr`.
